audit.whatIsWrong: Page reads TRICKY 7/10 while the mirror set the Graves page to UNFAV 7/10 — i.e. Graves is the unfavoured side. Win rate is 56%.
audit.why: Ratings invert across the mirror, so an unfavoured Graves must appear here as a favoured Lillia. Both signals agree: 56% over 25 games, and a packet chart that gives Lillia five of seven stages.
audit.corrected: FAV, 3.5/10, tone moved to the favoured green.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart on disk (Graves/Graves/Graves/Graves/Skill/Skill/Skill in BOTH layers) is the exact inverse of the packet and of every why-string on the page.
audit.why: whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6] all describe Lillia winning those stages, and whys[4] is the one Graves stage. The prose was right and the enums were wrong on six of seven rows. The mirror has already rewritten both charts on the Graves page as one group, so this side has to move with it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill/Lillia/Lillia/Lillia/Graves/Lillia/Lillia in both layers, ratings inverted to match, and all seven full-layer why strings rewritten so the prose stops arguing the old chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings say Smoke Screen blinds.
audit.why: Riot's text: it 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range', and enemies caught in the initial impact take magic damage and are slowed briefly. There is no blind. A Lillia player who thinks she is blinded plays it as a damage denial when it is actually a vision denial she can walk out of — and the slow on impact, which is the part that actually catches her, goes unmentioned. The mirror made the same correction.
audit.corrected: Sight-range cut and the impact slow named; 'blind' removed everywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Graves' bullets cannot pass through units.
audit.why: Riot's passive text is explicit: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Standing behind the minion wave physically eats his damage — the single strongest free mitigation Lillia has in this lane, and it is absent from the page. The page also calls it a 'two-bullet burst'; it is four.
audit.corrected: Written into wants.you[1] and the early paragraph.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is treated as a plain dash with 'charges'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 425-range dash on 16/15/14/13/12 granting Armor and MR, TWO stacks of True Grit if he dashes toward a champion, and hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resistances. So the resist boost is not a one-off — he sustains it by auto-attacking, which is why bursting him mid-trade underperforms.
audit.corrected: Real cooldown, the auto-attack refresh and the resist boost written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], dosFull[0].d and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states the Dream Dust precondition on Lilting Lullaby, or its 150s rank-1 cost.
audit.why: Riot's text Drowsies only 'enemies with Dream Dust on them'. Against a champion who can Quickdraw out of the Drowsy window, knowing you must land Q or E first is the whole play.
audit.corrected: Precondition and the 150s cost written into whys[4], spikes[1], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet defect: none of Graves's abilities were named in the content layer.
audit.why: 'His E dash', 'W smoke', 'shotgun autos' is exactly the vagueness the bar exists to remove — and in this case the vagueness hid two outright errors.
audit.corrected: New Destiny, Smoke Screen, Quickdraw and Lilting Lullaby named at their real slots.

edits.before: Level 1 you concede — you only have Q and Graves' shotgun auto chunks you, so just farm Q from max range and eat nothing. The lane flips at 2-3: once your Q sweetspot starts stacking move speed and your E slow lands, you become uncatchable and the Dream Dust burn ticks every time he steps up to auto. Bait his two-bullet burst, then chase on your speed stacks — he has to reload, and that reload window is when your DoT is free damage he can't shoot back.
edits.after: Level 1 you concede — you only have Q and Graves' shotgun chunks you, so farm Q from max range and eat nothing. The lane flips at 2-3: once Blooming Blows starts stacking move speed and Swirlseed lands, you become uncatchable and Dream Dust ticks every time he steps up to auto. His attacks fire four bullets and then he must reload — bait the burst, chase on your speed stacks, and that reload window is free DoT damage he cannot shoot back.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your takeover: full-rank Q, the burn compounding, and enough mana to grind him down on every step-up. Stay glued to him on your move-speed stacks so his E dash can't open the gap, and keep E up to re-slow if he flashes the distance. Level 6 is his window, not yours — your Lilting Lullaby sleep is delayed and he can E-in plus W-blind your follow-up to all-in you, so hold R for anti-engage or a jungler setup rather than a solo pick, and never get caught mid-kite with your E on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your takeover: full-rank Q, the burn compounding, and enough mana to grind him on every step-up. Stay glued to him on your move-speed stacks so Quickdraw — 16 seconds at rank 1, and it refreshes off his autos — can't open the gap, and keep Swirlseed up to re-slow. Level 6 is his window: Lilting Lullaby costs 150 seconds and only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust, and he can Quickdraw in behind Smoke Screen's sight cut, so hold R for anti-engage or a jungler setup, never a solo pick.

notes: This page's level chart was the exact inverse of the packet on six of seven rows in BOTH layers, while every content why-string argued the packet version — the enums had drifted, not the prose. All fourteen chart edits (seven sides x two layers) plus the seven ratings are proposed together as one atomic group. Two factual corrections worth flagging to the user: Smoke Screen does not blind (it cuts sight range and slows on impact), and Graves' four bullets cannot pass through units, so the minion wave is real mitigation — neither fact was anywhere on the page.
